subject: Environment binding & risk prioritization for ClearCare MAP
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@clearcare.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearcare.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP: environment binding questions before exec review

Hi Logan / Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Leadership wants a concise recommendation for the exec review next week on two things we need to lock in: 1) whether we run in Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC), and 2) which region(s) we should bind to for initial rollout given our PHI scope.

High level constraints from our side:
- Data residency: patient data must remain in US regions for the pilot
- Throughput: peak inference during processing windows ~60 req/s (95th percentile)
- Procurement: Dedicated would require a three-month commitment approval

Can you share a short risk-prioritized list (3 items) for each option (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) that we can paste into the MAP slide deck? Also attach any suggested gating criteria for the eval phase.

Appreciate it — Sam

--
Sam Jenkins
Director, Product Operations
ClearCare Health
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@clearcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: environment binding questions before exec review

Thanks Sam — good summary. I ran this by the team and sketched a short risk-prioritized bullet list and the eval gates we recommend. See below; I added a quick recommendation at the top.

Recommendation (short): Start in Hosted (US region) for speed of onboarding and to validate behaviour under production-like traffic. If by the end of the 6-week eval we hit sustained 50–60 req/s with >100ms p95 improvement target unmet or if residency/legal requires dedicated perimeter, move to Dedicated (reserved capacity in US-east) with a short private beta for the sensitive workloads. Private (on-prem) only if the compliance team cannot sign an exception — high M&P cost and long lead time.

Risk-prioritized bullets (top 3 each) — quick view:
Hosted:
- Risk: Data residency audit questions (mitigant: regional hosting in US-east + customer-specific retention policy).
- Risk: Burst traffic hitting soft limits (mitigant: pre-approved burst capacity and autoscale policy in MAP).
- Risk: SLA variations for dedicated compute workloads (mitigant: fallback to cached variants and rate limiting).

Dedicated:
- Risk: Procurement lead time (mitigant: parallel legal & SOW drafting in week 2 of MAP).
- Risk: Cost commit vs uncertain steady-state traffic (mitigant: staged capacity reservation + 30% headroom).
- Risk: Slightly longer deployment and rollback surface (mitigant: canary routing between dedicated and hosted).

Private (on-prem / VPC):
- Risk: Integration & network ingress complexity (mitigant: pre-approved networking runbook + Redwood Private engineer support).
- Risk: Long provisioning and validation window (mitigant: vendor-managed image and infra templates; expect 8–12 week runway).
- Risk: Ongoing ops burden for tuning and kernel selection (mitigant: Redwood Optimize engagement + quarterly review).

Suggested Eval Gates (to include in the MAP):
- Gate 1 (Week 2): Security questionnaire closed + baseline latency test in US region (p50/p95).
- Gate 2 (Week 4): Throughput smoke test at 60 req/s sustained for 15m; cost projection validated.
- Gate 3 (Week 6): Legal residency confirmation or formal exception; SLA target validated.

I can formalize these into a one-slide risk matrix and drop the updated MAP spreadsheet. Marissa, want me to draft the slide or should we let you take the exec-facing wording?

— Logan
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@clearcare.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: environment binding questions before exec review

Adding a couple of operational notes from the Console/Optimize side that affect risk prioritization:

- For Hosted we can enable prefix caching and auto-batching which should reduce token cost by ~18% in typical clinical flows; that helps justify initial Hosted recommendation.
- Dedicated gives us deterministic p95 on most model families — important if their SLAs for response time are strict. We should capture a target p95 (e.g., <250ms) as a success metric in the MAP.
- For Private, note that KMS integrations will require a separate key policy review; that will add ~2 weeks to the security gate.

Also attaching a short Monte Carlo of cost sensitivity for the three modes (I will add numbers to the MAP file).

— Grace
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: environment binding questions before exec review

Tech quick note for the evaluation plan: if we run Hosted for the initial 6-week MAP, we should instrument a KV-cache hit-rate probe and a sequence-length distribution sample at week 1 and week 3. Those two telemetry points usually predict whether Dedicated will be needed later.

Also: for Dedicated we can pre-build an image (quantized runtime + kernels) to shorten the dedicated provisioning by ~10 days if procurement signs the LOI in week 1.

Attachment references: ClearCare_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP workbook; tab 2 = gating criteria), clearcare-security-summary.pdf (one-pager with KMS/QS details).

— Dev

Subject: Re: MAP: environment binding questions before exec review

Sam —

Thanks — attaching the MAP workbook (ClearCare_MAP_v3.xlsx) and security summary PDF. The workbook has:
- Executive recommendation (short) 
- Risk matrix you can paste into the slide deck (Hosted-first, Dedicated fallback, Private last resort)
- Gate definitions and success metrics (Week 2/4/6)

Ask: can you confirm procurement is comfortable with an LOI in week 1 as discussed? If procurement needs longer, we should note that in the exec brief as a lead-time risk.

If no objections I will publish the slide and sync with Logan to finalize wording by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
